title: A reproducible framework for evaluating closed-loop embedding-drift recovery (with two evaluation-design hazards)
description: Open framework for evaluating detection-triggered, bounded, post-hoc correction loops over a retrieval store under controlled seeded drift. Includes a deterministic drift injector (manifest-level reproducibility), a recovery-trajectory metric suite, and a pre-registered protocol. Surfaces two evaluation-design hazards backed by runtime evidence: (1) the C2-oracle hazard — re-embedding with the original frozen encoder is a degenerate oracle for synthetic geometric drift, not a fair maintenance baseline; (2) the supervision-signal mechanism — an unsupervised homeostatic loop's loss-optimal correction is near-identity, so recovery requires an explicit pre-drift supervision channel. Includes a worked partial-recovery example on SciFact and NFCorpus in an encoder-upgrade arena. STAGED ARTIFACT — operator must confirm license/author and pull final numbers before upload.
